youtube.title: Why Ships Have Red Bottoms 🚢 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Many large ships have red paint below the waterline. It is antifouling paint, usually containing copper compounds such as cuprous oxide, which gives the red color. The copper slowly leaches into the water and stops barnacles, algae and weeds from sticking to the hull. A fouled hull creates drag, so the ship would burn far more fuel.
